t: The 1994 amendment to the MV Act added which sections on structured formula compensation?
e: The 1994 amendment covered hazardous goods and inserted Sections 163A and 163B for structured formula compensation; 163A is now Section 164.

t: Which section of the Motor Tariff contains the statistical codes that insurers must use for data submission?
e: Section 8 contains statistical codes; GR-48 makes submission of statistics to TAC imperative under Section 64UE of the Insurance Act.

t: Under GR-49, clarifications and interpretations of the India Motor Tariff given by the TAC are
o: Binding only on public sector insurers
e: GR-49 makes the Tariff Advisory Committee's interpretations final and binding.

t: A learner's licence is valid for
e: Learner's licences are valid for 6 months; the minimum age depends on the class of vehicle.

t: The minimum age for a transport vehicle driving licence is
e: Transport vehicle licences require a minimum age of 20 years, no learner's licence and one year's holding of an LMV licence.

t: A driver whose licence has been revoked under Section 19 gets it back at the end of the disqualification period only if he
o: Successfully completes the driver refresher training course
e: The licence is returned only on successful completion of the refresher training course from a licensed school or notified agency.

t: Under Section 44, a vehicle sold by an authorised dealer, for first registration,
o: Need not be produced before the registering authority
Must be produced before the RTO within 7 days
Must be inspected by an insurer's surveyor
Must be produced at an automated testing station
e: Section 44 dispenses with production of a dealer-sold vehicle before the registering authority for first registration.

t: Metal parts worth ₹40,000 are replaced on a car aged 3 years 8 months. The depreciation deducted on these parts is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). For a vehicle above 3 years but below 4 years, depreciation on metal parts is 25%, i.e. ₹10,000.

t: Under Section 62B, no RC may be issued or renewed unless it has a unique registration number under the
e: The 2019 amendment created a National Register of Motor Vehicles subsuming the State registers.

t: Under Section 56, if the prescribed authority cancels a fitness certificate, the RC and permit of the vehicle are
o: Deemed suspended until a new fitness certificate is obtained
e: On cancellation of fitness, the RC and any permit are deemed suspended until a new certificate of fitness is obtained.

t: Under Section 83, a permit holder may replace the vehicle on the same permit
o: Only on sale of the old vehicle
With the permission of the RTO
e: Replacement of a vehicle on an existing permit requires the RTO's permission.

t: The minimum qualifications for a conductor's licence under Section 30 are
e: Conductor's licence requires 18 years of age, 8th standard pass and medical fitness.

t: Under Section 130, a driver must on demand produce documents for examination to
e: Section 130 obliges the driver/conductor to produce licence, insurance, fitness and permit on demand by a police officer in uniform.

t: The 'contribution' condition of the motor policy provides that where another policy covers the same liability, the insurer pays
o: Nothing until the other insurer pays
The full claim and recovers from the other insurer
Its ratable proportion of compensation, costs and expenses
e: The insurer contributes a ratable proportion where more than one policy covers the same liability.

t: Which condition requires the insured to take all reasonable steps to safeguard the vehicle from loss and keep it in efficient condition?
e: The maintenance condition requires the insured to keep the vehicle in effective condition and safeguard it after an accident.

t: OD premium on a private car is ₹6,000 and the insured is an Automobile Association member. The AA discount allowed is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GR-28 allows 5% of OD premium (₹300) subject to a maximum of ₹200 for cars (₹50 for two wheelers).

t: Private car cover under the standard policy extends to use for the insured's professional purposes but excludes
o: Carriage of goods other than samples
e: Professional use is covered excluding carriage of goods other than samples, and excluding hire or reward, racing, speed testing, reliability trials and motor trade.

t: Loss arising while the vehicle is used in Pakistan without geographical extension is excluded under
e: Loss outside the geographical area (India, unless extended under GR-4/IMT-1) is a general exclusion.

t: A goods carriage tows a disabled vehicle for reward. Under the limitations as to use this is
o: Excluded, as towing is permitted only other than for reward and for one disabled vehicle
e: Use whilst drawing a trailer is excluded except towing (not for reward) of any one disabled vehicle.

t: Which of the following Class D vehicles can be given cover under a non-motor policy for risks other than road liability?
e: Bull dozers, bull graders, mobile cranes, excavators, fork lifts, drilling rigs and mobile plant may be covered under non-motor policies; milk vans and tankers are GCCV.

t: When a vehicle is ferried by sea to Sri Lanka under a GR-4 extension, damage during the sea voyage is
e: GR-4 excludes damage to vehicle, injury to occupants and TP liability during air passage or sea voyage for ferrying the vehicle to the extended area.

t: A policy for a period shorter than 12 months to align with a convenient renewal date is permitted under GR-11
o: On pro-rata basis subject to conditions and a warranty
e: GR-11 allows shorter duration for arriving at a particular renewal date on pro-rata basis subject to conditions and a warranty; other short periods attract short period rates.

t: Under GR-34, a vehicle may be insured in a name different from the registered owner only in case of
o: Temporary substitution, motor trade risk, or hire purchase/lease/hypothecation per GR 19-21
e: GR-34 bars insuring in a name not matching the RC, with exceptions for temporary substitution, motor trade risks and GR-19/20/21 situations.

t: A brand new car has an ex-showroom listed price of ₹10,00,000 and is 3 months old at renewal. Its IDV as per schedule is
e: IDV depreciation for a vehicle not exceeding 6 months is 5%, giving ₹9,50,000.

t: The IDV depreciation schedule does NOT apply to
o: Brand new vehicles under motor trade policies
e: GR-8: no depreciation applies to brand new vehicles covered under motor trade policies.

t: Under the partial loss depreciation table, parts of a vehicle aged 4 years 6 months attract
e: The band above 4 years but below 5 years carries 35% depreciation on metal and other parts.

t: Repair bill: labour ₹10,000, metal parts ₹20,000, rubber parts ₹4,000 on a car aged 1 year 8 months. Depreciation deducted is
e: Metal parts at 1-2 years attract 10% (₹2,000); rubber parts 50% (₹2,000); labour carries no depreciation; total ₹4,000.

t: Under the survey fee schedule w.e.f. 01.10.2022, the fee for a repair estimate of ₹3,00,000 is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). For estimates between ₹2 lakh and ₹30 lakh the fee is ₹2,800 plus 0.70% on the balance above ₹2 lakh: 2,800 + 700 = ₹3,500.

t: The minimum value for premium computation of a private car not exceeding 1000 cc is
e: Minimum values are ₹15,000 (up to 1000 cc), ₹20,000 (1000-1500 cc) and ₹30,000 (above 1500 cc) for private cars.

t: For a two wheeler exceeding 350 cc the minimum value for premium purposes is
e: Two wheeler minimum values are ₹5,000 (up to 150 cc), ₹6,000 (150-350 cc) and ₹7,000 (above 350 cc).

t: The annual Liability Only premium for a private car exceeding 1500 cc w.e.f. 01.06.2022 is
e: TP rates from 01.06.2022: ₹2,094 (up to 1000 cc), ₹3,416 (1000-1500 cc), ₹7,897 (above 1500 cc); ₹24,596 is the 3-year long term rate.

t: Long term TP premium for a new two wheeler of 125 cc for five years is
e: The 5-year long term TP rate for two wheelers above 75 cc up to 150 cc is ₹3,851.

t: OD premium ₹20,000 with 5 completed claim-free years. The insured now submits a claim. On next renewal the NCB will be
e: Once a claim arises NCB reverts to nil (unless an NCB protection add-on was opted); the 50% applies only to the current renewal.

t: The maximum anti-theft device discount per policy under GR-30 is
e: 2.5% of OD premium subject to a maximum of ₹500; the ₹200 cap applies to the AA membership discount.

t: Under GR-33, vehicles specially modified for blind or handicapped persons get a 50% OD discount provided
o: The owner holds a disability certificate
The vehicle is owned by an NGO
The RC is suitably endorsed by the RTA
e: The discount applies to privately owned and institutional vehicles only when the RC is endorsed by the RTA concerned (IMT-12).

t: Lay-up concession under GR-31 is NOT available for
o: Vehicles used for hire or reward
e: No premium return is allowed for lay-up of trailers, vehicles used for hire and reward or vehicles used for motor trade.

t: Under the IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) Regulations 2024, the free-look period for a policy with a term of one year or more is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 30 days from receipt of the policy document, irrespective of the sales channel.

t: Compulsory PA cover bundled with the motor policy ceased to be mandatory with effect from
e: From 01.01.2019 the owner-driver may take a standalone CPA cover of ₹15 lakh valid for all his vehicles instead of bundling it.

t: A three wheeler rated as a private car with engine capacity 1200 cc has a compulsory deductible of
e: Private cars including three wheelers rated as private cars carry ₹1,000 below 1500 cc and ₹2,000 above.

t: Under the compulsory deductible table, vehicles rated under Class E, F and G of the CVT carry a deductible of
o: ₹50 for two wheelers and ₹250 for others
₹100 for two wheelers and ₹500 for others
e: The GR-40 table shows ₹100 for two wheelers and ₹500 for other vehicles under motor trade classes (the overview slide quotes ₹50/₹500 for Class G).

t: Which document is required for a commercial vehicle accident claim but not for a private car claim?
e: Commercial vehicle claims additionally need fitness certificate, permit and authorisation, taxation book, load challan/trip sheet and spot survey report.

t: For commercial vehicle and large risk claims, the surveyor must submit the final report within
e: The general time limit is 30 days, extended to 90 days from appointment for commercial vehicle and large risk claims.

t: Under the regulations summarised by the trainer, the insurer may seek clarification from the surveyor on his report
o: Any number of times within 30 days
e: Clarification may be sought once within 15 days and the surveyor's additional report must come within 3 weeks.

t: Under the 2024 master circular as cited, surveyor allocation is to be done within 24 hours through
o: A tech-based solution on a random basis
e: The circular requires random, technology-based allocation of surveyors within 24 hours of intimation.

t: Under the battery protect add-on, a claim is excluded where the battery was replaced at
o: A workshop not authorised by the OEM
The insured's residence by OEM technician
e: Repairs or replacement at a workshop not authorised by the OEM, non-standard charging, unauthorised swapping and warranty-covered losses are excluded.

t: An Insurance Ombudsman can entertain a complaint where the value of the claim, including expenses, does not exceed:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The limit was raised to ₹50 lakh by the amended Insurance Ombudsman Rules.

t: Under a Motor Trade Transit Risk policy, the 50% limitation on tyres can be deleted to pay 100% because
o: Tyres are not covered at all
The vehicles and their tyres are new
e: Since vehicles in transit from the manufacturer are new, the 50% tyre limitation can be deleted on payment of additional premium.

t: Under Section 147 of the MV Act, a policy of insurance is of no effect unless the insurer issues
o: A certificate of insurance in the prescribed form
A policy schedule countersigned by the RTO
e: Section 147(3) makes the certificate of insurance in the prescribed form essential; Section 156 treats the certificate as the full policy.

t: Where a cover note is not followed by a policy within the specified time, the insurer must notify the registering authority within
o: 7 days of expiry of the cover note
e: Section 147(5) requires notification to the registering authority within seven days of expiry of the cover note's validity.

t: An appeal from the District Commission to the State Commission must be filed within
o: 30 days, with deposit of 50% of the award
45 days, with deposit of 50% of the award
e: Appeal to the State Commission lies within 30 days with 50% deposit; to the National Commission within 45 days with 50% deposit.
